pr_title: [ML] Make model snapshot upgrade autoscaling friendly
pr_body:
Model snapshot upgrade was not taking autoscaling into account
when doing node assignment.

Fixes #81012

issue_context.title: [ML] upgrade model snapshot is not autoscaling-friendly
issue_context.body:
Steps to reproduce: 
1. In a 7.6 cloud cluster, create and start a machine learning AD job. 
2. After job finished and stopped, upgrade the job to 7.16
3. Enable the autoscaling
4. Wait several minutes, and make sure there is no jobs running and no ml node in the plan (because of autoscaling ON)
5. In kibana, go to upgrade assistant, you should see warning about obsolete minimum version of model snapshot
6. In dev tools, fire an upgrade snapshot request: `POST _ml/anomaly_detectors/<job>/model_snapshots/<snapshot id>/_upgrade` 

Observed:
an error message says: `Could not open job because no ML nodes with sufficient capacity were found`. Also,  no ml node is provisioned after several minutes waiting.

Expected:
Upgrade model snapshot should be autoscaling-aware, ml node should be provisioned.
comments:
This is because we don't treat the snapshot upgrade tasks the same as anomaly detection tasks. 

Honestly, I am not 100% sure we should autoscale in this scenario. If they have zero ML nodes, that means they are not running ML at all and probably just have an old snapshot that they forgot about and need to delete. It seems weird to autoscale to me.

The change isn't too difficult (simply catch the upgrade snapshot tasks with the anomaly detection tasks).

> Honestly, I am not 100% sure we should autoscale in this scenario.

The situation of needing to scale from 0 to 1 for model snapshot upgrade is extreme - really just a way to test the scenario of needing to autoscale.

But I think needing to scale to a bigger node definitely needs to work.  The model snapshot upgrade processes are going to need about as much memory as the corresponding job, as they're instantiating the same object structure in memory.  So if autoscaling has made the cluster as small as it can be to run the current jobs then it's highly likely that a model snapshot upgrade won't also fit.

> The change isn't too difficult (simply catch the upgrade snapshot tasks with the anomaly detection tasks).

I'm just working through this now.

review_comments:
Fixing this isn't what this PR is primarily about, but I noticed it while debugging the new test, so thought it worth documenting.  The way all our sliding scales interact is very complex.  We should refactor this once the formula for node size to JVM size is reversible.

To be more accurate this method also needs to know the maximum ML node size and the principle that Cloud always scales up before scaling out.  Maximum ML node size is not currently reliably set.  But work is in progress to make it accurate, and this will take effect no later than the delegation of the JVM heap size to Elasticsearch.

So in the next refactor all the prerequisites will be in place to make this better.

I moved `SnapshotUpgradeTaskParams` into the `core` plugin so that it's accessible to `MlTasksTests`.  It used to be in the same package as `SnapshotUpgradePredicate` so could be used without importing but now it's not.
It is used in this file.  It used to be in the same package but isn't now.
